x: A programme of three events gave only a few of our Juniors a chance to show their merit; but Mewes, Crilly, Keyworth, Dyke, Martin, Chantler and Clements certainly seized the opportunity to show their superiority over the other clubs.

Of the sprinters, Brodie and Kealey have been prominent, with Wiley coming along nicely, and others such as Basford and Stroud (until his leg "gave way") of the seniors, and Mewes, the Crillys, Bennett and others of the younger brigade, keeping up their average.

Mewes was fourth in the 100 yards, Page being the winner. In the 4 x 220 yards we were fourth (Mewes, Bennett, Stower, Christie), a position we also filled in the 4 x 440 yards event (Jones, Stower, Clubb, Pack).
Alec Mewes, another with promise, ran out a narrow winner in the 220 yards handicap, and a third young man, Percy Wright, experienced the pleasure of breaking the tape for the first time in the Walk.

On May 25th, at the White City, was held the 4 x 220 yds. and we fielded a useful team in Kealey, Stroud, Mewes and Michael. Kealey elected to start for us, and drawing number 1 station, he was twice bumped very badly and so we lost any advantage which we might have had.
Unfortunately, and I say that advisedly, we were without the sprinters we had been relying upon, and so our team for the 4 x 100 was Mewes, Bennet, Michael and Camkin.
We (the Belgrave Harriers) would also like to see some of the older members back in training, such as Messrs. Bone, Mewes, Kealey and Co. The Club has many promising juniors also.
Skelley, Mewes, Pritchard and Blunden, who formed the team. (Congratulations also to Skelley on having his shorts passed by a Southern A.A.A. representative!).
A Belgrave team of Dyke, Bone and Mewes was entered. Evidently it was a regular race as previous times of 10.8 etc are given and winners had been Poly and Blackheath.
